title: Lateral Onboarding Activation Checklist + Tech Probe
summary: A practical, lightweight playbook for activating lateral hires (external senior ICs or cross-functional transfers) into engineering teams. Emphasizes a non-duplicative technical probe, role-aligned 7/30/60/90 checklists, manager and buddy responsibilities, early-success metrics, and compliance/security gates.
body:
Purpose:
This doc outlines a repeatable activation flow for lateral hires joining engineering as ICs (senior, staff-level, or product-to-eng transfers). Goal: reduce ambiguity, set clear signal-forwarding expectations, and validate role fit with minimal friction — avoid long take-homes that duplicate onsite interviews; prefer short, guided technical probes and observation-based assessments.

Scope:
- Applies to external hires at L4+ joining eng teams and internal transfers into eng from product/infra/business teams.
- Not prescriptive for junior/new-grad onboarding or manager onboarding (separate playbooks).
- Assumes baseline HR tasks (offer, payroll, hardware request) are handled by People Ops/IT.

Key Principles:
1) Low-friction signal generation: one 3-hour bounded technical probe or pair-programming session + code reading exercise, not a 48-hour take-home.
2) Role alignment: probes emphasize the specific responsibilities they'll own (infra, latency, model serving, API design, reliability).
3) Observation over contrived tasks: prioritize paired work on a real repository slice to see collaboration and judgement.
4) Early wins: surface 1-2 low-risk tasks they can own in the first 30 days.
5) Clear success metrics and escalation points for manager and buddy.

Pre-start checklist (People Ops / Hiring Manager / IT)
- People Ops: final welcome packet sent, first-day schedule, onboarding playlist, Slack invite created.
- IT: laptop imaged, corp VPN & MFA accounts provisioned, developer accounts (GitHub, CI, cloud) requested.
- Security: background check completed per policy; code access scope pre-approved for probe environment.
- Hiring Manager: 7-day plan and 30-day objective drafted and shared; assigned peer-buddy identified.

Day 0 / First day (manager + buddy)
- Quick orientation 45–60min: team intro, org chart, immediate communication norms, short product overview (15m).
- Repo tour: buddy walks through the primary repo, CI flow, deploy basics (30–45m).
- Admin: access checks (can push to sandbox branch, can run local tests).
- First tiny task assigned (<2 hours) that results in an end-to-end signal (e.g., add a logging flag, fix a flaky test).

7-day checklist (outcomes manager should confirm)
- Can run local dev environment and CI for core service(s).
- Successfully merged at least one change to a non-production sandbox branch.
- Completed the technical probe (see probe section) and debriefed with hiring panel.
- Buddy and manager have given initial feedback; any tooling blockers logged to IT.

Technical Probe (recommended pattern)
- Timebox: 2–3 hours total across activities.
- Structure: 30–45min repo walkthrough and context handoff; 60–90min pair-programming or sandbox task; 30min debrief with hiring manager and one technical lead.
- Scope: focused on code-reading, small unit of implementable logic (e.g., implement a robust input validation and a low-cost memoization layer, or fix a performance regression in a small endpoint).
- Environment: use a dedicated ephemeral sandbox repo or branch that mirrors production wiring but never contains PII or customer data.
- Evaluation: rubric-based notes (see interview rubric section) — emphasize design tradeoffs, testability, communication, and risk awareness.
- Outcome paths: pass -> proceed with standard onboarding; borderline -> 30-day paired mentorship and targeted learning plan; fail -> hiring manager + People Ops discuss remedial options (rare).

Coding/Behavior Rubric (one-page, used live during probe)
- Problem Understanding (1–5): clarified constraints, asked good Qs, scoped appropriately.
- Tradeoff Reasoning (1–5): articulated latency/cost/operational tradeoffs and alternatives.
- Implementation Quality (1–5): correctness, test coverage, simplicity.
- Collaboration (1–5): pairs well, responsive to prompts, ownership language.
- Safety & Security Awareness (1–5): considered edge cases, input validation, secrets handling.
- Overall Recommendation: Hire / Hire with Mentorship / Needs More Evidence.

30-day checklist (owner: manager)
- Clear 30-day objective met: usually a shipped small feature, bug fix, or reliability improvement.
- First on-call shadowing completed (if role requires).
- Engaged in at least two design discussions and given a voiced opinion.
- Feedback loop: 1:1 frequency confirmed; first 30-day sync scheduled with People Ops and manager.
- Development plan for next 60 days defined (training resources, mentor pairing, stretch tasks).

60-day checklist
- Ownership: owning a module, test suite, or operational runbook.
- Quality signals: code review rate, PR size, and post-deploy rollback frequency within team norms.
- Behavior: demonstrated cross-team communication and escalations handled appropriately.
- Calibration: manager provides midpoint calibration; if borderline, escalate to People Ops for an intervention plan.

90-day checklist and success criteria
- Delivered at least one medium-scope item end-to-end or a measurable reliability improvement.
- Peer feedback aggregated (3+ peers) shows readiness level for role band expectations.
- Manager recommendation: continue as IC / continue with mentorship / role adjustment.

Manager & Buddy responsibilities (concise)
- Manager: set expectations, own objectives, remove blockers, conduct formal 30- and 90-day reviews.
- Buddy: daily check-ins first week, weekly pairing sessions first 30 days, sandbox PR reviews, cultural navigation.

Special considerations for internal transfers (product -> eng)
- Emphasize code reading and testing fluency rather than algorithmic puzzles.
- Probe weight reduced: focus on collaboration signal and product-to-implementation translation.
- Provide a 30-day plan that leverages product-domain knowledge (fast path to impact).

Security & compliance gates
- No production credentials in probe environment.
- Access to customer data requires explicit approval and audit logging.
- If role handles regulated data, complete compliance UAT checklist before granting full access.

Early success metrics (observable signals)
- 7d: can run tests, open PRs, merge a sandbox change.
- 30d: merged a production-bounded change with peer review and no major reverts.
- 60d: owning an oncall rotation or runbook and a measurable reduction in MTTR for owned service.
- 90d: independent delivery of medium-scope work and positive peer calibration.

Escalation flow (if onboarding stalls)
- Week 2 blockers: manager + buddy + IT meeting to remediate access/tooling.
- At 30 days not meeting objectives: formal remediation plan with People Ops and a named mentor.
- At 60 days still below expectations: people-ops-facilitated calibration meeting (include hiring manager, technical lead, and HR) to decide next steps.

Template messages (copy/paste)
- Welcome DM to team: "Hi team — please welcome {name}, joining as {title} on {start_date}. Buddy: {buddy}. First-day plan pinned in #onboarding."
- Probe invite to candidate: "We'd like to schedule a 2.5-hour activation session: 30m repo context, 90m paired work, 30m debrief. We'll provide a sandbox repo and a short pre-read. Are you available {options}?"

Appendix: Examples of 90–180 minute probe tasks
- Implement a resilient input sanitizer and a small caching layer; add tests and a brief note on tradeoffs.
- Pair-debug a flaky integration test and land a small fix with explanation.
- Read an existing feature PR and outline 3 follow-up improvements and a deployment checklist.

Notes / Open questions:
- Should we standardize a single sandbox repo across teams? Pros: consistency; Cons: losing domain-specific signals.
- Timing: allow candidate to choose morning or afternoon sessions to respect personal productivity windows.
